Some people insist that they have to admit this phenomenon as part of their fame. However, I strongly disagree with this opinion. This is because famous people have a right to have private space in their lives and they might be victims of criminals.



To begin with, eminent people have a right to have their own space in their daily lives. In fact, everyone needs a private room where they can be protected from external factors including famous people. Having a boundary plays a pivotal role in people's lives. When people's rights are invaded by other elements, they might be able to have mental issues such as depression, anxiety, and so on. To cite an example, some celebrities in South Korea struggle with their mental problems since they do not have enough space for their schedule. They protest to media companies to stop posting their life in order to tackle this problem. Sometimes, they have medicines or conduct sessions to deal with their stress. Moreover, This situation might lead their fandoms to have a sense of worry and a lot of entertainment companies to lose their assets as prominent people in our society.



In addition, celebrities might be able to become victims of awful people. The number of criminals has been increasing nowadays, some people, called a stoker, cross the private rooms. They are more likely to invade eminent people's daily lives by following their schedules every single day and taking a majority of pictures. Sometimes, they even attack celebrities physically. For example, there was a serious crime in China. One prominent actress, named Wan Wei was captured by a stoker. The criminal said that he was able to check her life by watching media news all the time. This means that too much information about celebrities' lives might cause detrimental situations for them such as stoking, captures, and so on.



To sum up, it is evident that some people reckon that they deserve to monitor celebrities' lives because of their fame. However, I totally disagree with it, since famous people have a right to have their boundaries and might be targeted by criminals.

task2.prompt: Some people believe that the main benefit of international cooperation is the protection of the environment, while others think that the main benefits are in the world of business. Discuss both views and give your opinion
task2.sample:
People have different views as to whether the environment or the world’s economy and businesses benefit most from global cooperation. Personally, I contend that the latter is more likely to enjoy fruitful results from this trend.



One the one hand, when the world becomes a global village, environmental protection turns out to be a common concern and is addressed on a global scale. Kyoto Protocol, which is an international treaty that imposes limitations on CO2 emissions on member nations, helps to reduce a significant amount of the gas into the atmosphere. Were this treaty not brought to life by concerted efforts of many nations, our carbon footprint would be much greater and the damage we did to our planet would be more severe. Moreover, given countries are inexorably linked to each other economically and politically, the wealthier ones could introduce environmentally linked aid to poorer countries with a view to curb their uncontrolled paces of industrialization. Whatever the results of these practices, at least collective attempts made worldwide brings a great impact on individual consciousness, which prompts individuals to act environmentally responsibly.



However, I believe that economic prosperity is the main by-product of global integration. Thanks to an increasingly free global market, a number of undeveloped nations are being lifted out of poverty through either exporting their strengths or foreign investments. This is not likely to happen in times of political isolation had been the norm since the flows of goods, money, and humans were limited within national boundaries or regional borders. Furthermore, global cooperation enables transnational or international corporations to locate their manufacturing facilities on the other side of the world where cheap and abundant labours could make a huge difference in price production, leaving them an edge over their rivals.



In conclusion, I think, even though international cooperation could bring about some initiatives regarding environmental preservation it is the world of business that benefits most from the development.

People who consider creative activities such as drawing and painting should be taught at school may put forth the following argument. It is not easy to draw what you see on paper with a pen, so this process can improve hand-eye coordination skills. Moreover, there is no universal standard to judge a piece of art, therefore, if children are asked to learn how to draw at school, they will be encouraged to think outside the box, which can develop their creative thinking, and they can apply such skills to their future work or study. Last but not least is that such activities can find out people who are talented in the art field at an early age, thus helping them better recognize themselves and choose future career development in a wiser way.



However, opponents to this way of thinking have their own opinion, which they can also easily justify. Exams are usually required for courses at school, therefore, for those who have no talent for drawing, there will be no accomplishments they can gain through such courses, which may even make them feel depressed about school life. In addition, some parents may think the main responsibility for children at school is to work on academic knowledge rather than other art-related classes, such as drawing and painting, and most of them will not land jobs in the art industry, so it is unnecessary to study such courses while at school.



In conclusion, based on the above analysis and evidence, although some children may not derive direct benefits from learning how to draw, in my opinion, hand-eye coordination and creativity skills can be beneficial to them in their future lives.

To be specific, knowing about traditional habits allows people to have a good understanding of their own identity and preserve it through all generations. For example, on the Tet holiday in Vietnam, everyone will pay respect to their own ancestors by offering incense on the first day of the Lunar new year, which is a cultural tradition that Vietnamese people have followed for a long period of time. Hence, the study of history plays a paramount important part in making an all-rounded community by providing everyone with a great understanding of their culture. 



While the importance of studying the history of the family is widely acknowledged, it is unfair if focusing on the younger generations is ignored. To be particular, the offspring is the one that will follow and represent ancestors’ footsteps in the future. For instance, one of the most famous families in Thailand has owned various lucrative businesses and estates for more than 50 years. In fact, they relentlessly continue the plans and become more and more wealthy since the working styles of their ancestors are adapted and imitated by the youth. Hence, concentrating on the younger generations is also put priority in the development of the family's career.



To sum up, although looking back to family history acts as a paramount significant role in providing cultural tradition for everyone, laying stress on the young is of the essence in carrying the future career of a family.

 Firstly,It is reasonable to assume that one of the main driving forces behind the rise in online socializing is the advantage of social media in the last two decades. task2.prompt: nowadays, more and more jobs and tasks which involve hard physical work and done by machines. Do the positive effects of this trend outweith the negative effects?

In this technological era, much manual work, especially physically demanding work, can be carried out by machinery and robots. Although this trend has drawbacks, its advantages are much more significant.



On the one hand, we cannot deny that an increasing number of robotic workers lead to a climbing unemployment rate. Before the invention of computerised machines, industrial companies can always provide a considerable number of employment opportunities for low-skilled jobs such as porters and assemblers in factories while sometimes failing to hire enough people. Nowadays, in contrast, the number of such job positions is much less than before due to the popularity of automatic workers. As a result, an unthinkable group of people who do not have academic qualifications from universities find it difficult to find a job. 



On the other hand, the merits of this development totally outshine the aforementioned drawback. First of all, computers and computer-based technology have led to a much more streamlined and efficient workplace. Generally speaking, robot workers can work non-stop for 24 hours, whereas humans can only work for 8 hours according to labour law. In addition, computer-based calculation allows non-human machines to finish tasks without a single mistake. For that reason, the production cost can be largely minimised due to their outstanding work efficiency and great productivity. 



On top of that, people can prevent themselves from hurting themselves due to occupational hazards. Recent research from Chinese governments shows that in China, around 80,000 victims working in factories were injured or killed by incidents every year because of careless operations or unexpected coincidences. If machines undertake all the risky and heavy work, the number of such unfortunate tragedies would be considerably reduced.



To sum up. Although machine-based technologies result in a high unemployment rate, they ensure adequate productivity for businesses and the safety of individuals. Therefore, this improvement should be encouraged and developed.

Levying laws pertaining to people’s nutrition and food selection is conduce to making healthy residents, resulting in reducing pressure on a country’s healthcare system.  Plausible though it may seem that law can contain a person’s food habit, it is worth arguing that governments should not take any strides that would break the human right because an individual is solely responsible to improve his or her well-being. To be more precise, a person can choose many other ways, namely, doing workouts, weekly diet, to mention but a few with a view to keeping him or her fit as a fiddle. In conclusion, legislation can limit food habit, admittedly, but these laws violate the right of human. Thus, I unequivocally buttress the stand of not imposing laws about meal selection.

In conclusion, with a view to reducing the problem of obesity, it is necessary to do exercise and comprehend the downside of junk food.

task2.prompt:
Historical objects and artefacts should be brought back to their country of origin.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?
task2.sample:
The repatriation of historical objects and artefacts to their countries of origin has sparked intense debates. While I acknowledge the importance of preserving a nation's heritage and cultural identity, I believe that the decision to return these items should be made with careful consideration of various factors.



Firstly, repatriation can serve as a means to restore a sense of cultural pride and identity. Objects that hold historical and cultural significance often represent the heart of a nation's heritage, and their return can contribute to the enrichment of local communities. For instance, the return of the Elgin Marbles to Greece from the British Museum could enhance Greek citizens' connection to their ancient past, fostering a deeper appreciation for their own cultural roots.



However, the process of repatriation is not devoid of complexities. Museums and institutions that currently house these artefacts often argue that they have been responsible for their preservation, and returning them might jeopardise their conservation. Moreover, in cases where historical objects have been acquired through legal means or during times of colonial expansion, determining rightful ownership can be challenging. Repatriation could also hinder cultural exchange and global appreciation of history by limiting access to these objects from people around the world.



Striking a balance between repatriation and the preservation of global cultural heritage is crucial. Instead of blanket repatriation policies, collaboration between countries of origin and current custodians could be a more effective approach. This could involve temporary loans, joint exhibitions, or digital platforms to facilitate the sharing of information and knowledge about these objects.



In conclusion, while I agree that the return of historical objects and artefacts to their countries of origin can contribute positively to cultural identity, I also believe that a nuanced approach is necessary, with a focus on collaboration and compromise.

task2.prompt: Some people say that increasing business and cultural contacts between countries is a positive development, while others think that many countries will lose their national identities as a result. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
task2.sample:
There is no doubt that these days countries are increasing their trade and cultural connections. Some believe that it is a positive thing while others disagree with this idea. In this essay, I will discuss both points of view and I will share my personal opinion.



In terms of advantages, countries opening up to each other has many benefits. First, it made people understand and care for each other more. To illustrate, many recent reports showed an increase in tolerance among people in open societies. Secondly, multiple goods are now freely traded between the east and the west. This made those goods cheaper in price and more affordable. Gadgets and technology innovations spread immediately to be used all over the world.



On the other hand, while increasing connections between counties have its benefits, it also carries its own downsides. It turned the world into a global village. people can hardly differentiate between cities since most of them almost look and feel the same. In other words, travelling has lost most of its appeal. On top of that, small local businesses could not compete with large factories that are producing in China. Many of them could not maintain their businesses and had to close. In the long term, this is damaging to local economies.



In conclusion, although increasing cultural contact and opening up trade between countries is beneficial, it has its side effects. I believe that it is useful to increase business contact with some limits. I also believe that culture should be unique to each country and should be protected.

task2.prompt: In many countries, government likes to spend more money on the arts. Some people agree with this. However, other think that government should spend more on health and education. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.

On one side, some people assert that spending money on the artwork by the administrations is quite beneficial. Moreover, such financial support from government will encourage the youth to fulfil their dreams in this sector. On the other side, some folks believe that governments should give priority to finance hospitals and educational institutes. In conclusion, although spending money by administrations on art and skills give a platform to youth to develop their work, creativity, well-being and superior education are the need of the hour. task2.prompt: Some people think news has no connection to people’s lives. So, then it is a waste of time to read the newspaper and watch television news programs. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
task2.sample:
It is believed by some that reading newspapers and watching news programs on television is a waste of time since news seems to be irrelevant to human daily lives. In my opinion, I totally disagree with this view as I strongly argue that news plays a vital role in people’s lives these days.



First and foremost, I hold a firm belief that news is of vital importance in enhancing human beings’ living standards. This is because by keeping updated with the latest information, people can broaden their knowledge in many life aspects. This can be exemplified by some news programs about tips to have a healthy lifestyle. By watching such programs or reading healthcare articles, modern people can be aware of their unhealthy lifestyle, then form the right attitude towards a healthier way of life and ultimately lead a better life to maintain good physical and mental health. 



Besides, it is undeniable that news provides useful information for humans to become more proactive in dealing with unexpected situations on a daily basis. On a smaller scale, news about weather forecasts, for instance, can allow people to be well-prepared with raincoats or umbrellas before going out in order not to get wet and sick afterwards. Furthermore, news can also be of vital importance in more serious cases like the COVID-19 pandemic. In fact, thanks to the spreading power of news media, Vietnamese people can quickly have aware of the severity of the pandemic, so they take immediate actions to protect themselves and their family members from contagious risks by methods given on newspapers or TV news programs. As a result, Vietnam can fight against the COVID successfully and save many lives from death.



In conclusion, on account of the aforementioned reasons, I hold an argument that the role of news media in people’s daily lives is undoubtedly essential. It is highly recommended that people should utilize the news to make their life better and more connected to current affairs.

task2.prompt: In some cities and towns all over the world, the high volume of traffic is a problem. What are the causes of this and what actions can be taken to solve this problem?
task2.sample:
Voluminous traffic on the roads in urban areas has become a serious problem, in various countries across the globe. While there are myriads of contributing factors to this, over population and poor road infrastructure are the predominant ones. However, various positive measures, including; masses’ facilitation in rural regions and construction of new roads, can be taken by the government to eradicate this issue.
To begin with, there are several causes of hike in the vehicles in metropolitan regions. Firstly, with every passing day, urban areas are getting densely populated. Owing to the fact that cities are equipped with the advanced academic institutes, hospitals and organizations, individuals shift towards such areas. For instance, the United State population control department reported 65% average rise in the students of tertiary education in 2018. Consequently, with the growing inhabitants, transportation sources are escalating, which is the ultimate reason environmental contamination. Secondly, lack of basic roads and highways is the significant cause of traffic jams and congestions.
Nevertheless, the governmental bodies are liable to control the vehicles on the road. If the competent authorities provide the residents of the suburbs with the educational and earning resources in their hometowns, the former would have no reason to relocate in the towns. To illustrate, building new medical centres, universities, and establishment of companies in the countryside would benefit the masses at their doorsteps. Moreover, a suitable budget should be allocated to construct more roads and bridges to overcome the traffic flow.
To conclude, the proliferation in vehicles on roads due to the growing population and worst road conditions is becoming a major issue in both cities and towns. Therefore, the executive authorities must take steps to rectify this prevalent trend, by providing ease and comfort to the masses in rural regions. Furthermore, a fixed amount of the budget should be dedicated to the development of roads.

task2.prompt: Some believe that people should make efforts to fight climate change while others think it is better to learn to live with it. Discuss both views and give your own opinions.

Some human activities have negative effects on plant and animal species. Some people think it is too late to do anything about this problem while others think effective measures can be taken to improve this situation. Discuss both views and give your opinion
task2.sample:
Up to this day, the negative impacts of humans on the environment are actually evident. Besides, it is also debatable whether offering solutions to overcome this phenomenon has become too late or not. From my perspective, nature is still able to be ameliorated by our timely interventions. This essay will elaborate on my belief.



Perhaps for many, human beings’ destructive actions on the earth get out of control. First, in some cases, ecosystems have been severely degraded and it is almost impossible to restore them to their original state. To elaborate, the world is facing the mass extinction of numerous species due to habitat loss, which is supposed to be the result of industrialization and the greenhouse effect. Even worse, hunting also contributes to exacerbating this reality, for instance, the West African Black Rhinoceros was declared totally extinct in 2011 because many fool people believe its horns can cure some diseases. Second, there are several insolvable environmental problems that cannot be solved by an individual or even by a single country. To be specific, these include thawing due to climate change and seawater pollution from plastic waste, which damages the habitat of creatures in the Arctic and the ocean. In actuality, it is difficult for the actions of one nation or one person to have a significant impact on improving this situation.



Despite the valid arguments detailed above, I still believe that it is never too late to act. The most pertinent point is that numerous animal species which are on the brink of extinction need to be protected. People still constructively influence nature to protect plants and animals through habitat reinstatement as well as breeding projects. Many successful conservation stories demonstrate that it is possible to make a difference, such as the case of humpback whales. Another justification is that macro-environmental issues can be handled by the hand of the whole world. International cooperation can help create effective global movements in retaining biodiversity through public awareness campaigns and supporting environmental policies. Thus, the efforts of individuals will be multiplied and encouraged to alleviate environmental destruction.



To conclude, it is indisputable that humankind has caused a variety of harmful effects on our planet, which are irreversible or difficult to mitigate. Even so, I strongly agree with the positive view that there are a range of other parts of the world that can still be recovered if people strive to cure it.

The primary reason is that the house owner might come across a detail of the house that is bizarre or something they have never encountered before, which makes them curious. As a result, they start to do research about that detail and eventually find the information about their living space. For example, after watching a show about discovering ancient buildings, you might recognize that there is a chance that your house could have mystery and interesting stories while it was being constructed, which encourages you to start your journey exploring your house.

In conclusion, people can pick up seeking historical details about their living space for a variety of motives, namely curiosity and being influenced by documentation. And some solutions to accomplish this goal is to ask the seniors or to find references on your own.

Some people think that the detailed description of crimes on newspapers and TV has bad consequences, so this kind of information should be restricted in the media. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Some people embrace news on crimes as valuable safety reminders but others warn that they might incite crimes. In my opinion, while certain improvements are essential, restricting reports of this nature in the media should not be considered.



Despite the fact that social media today are increasingly used to attract viewers with threatening and exaggerated information about crimes which might create a bit of chaos in the readers’ minds, such reports still play a significant role in promoting local safety and perfecting legal systems. For example, news coverage often reveals crimes that would have otherwise been ignored or concealed from the public and administrators, igniting fierce discussions among local and online communities. This helps voice public concerns and encourages new regulations to be made. This is how the legal system is improved and safety is further secured.



Moreover, the conventional belief that coverage of crimes helps alert the public to lurking dangers still holds true in the current internet era. With the advancement of the internet, new forms of crime have emerged, which are completely unfamiliar to ordinary people. Online racketeering is a typical example, where a large amount of money could disappear with just a click on a cell phone or a conversation with strangers through smartphone applications. Unfortunately, these scenarios can change in just a few weeks or months, since criminals constantly come up with new swindles. In such cases, social media can never be too focused on updating crime information.



In conclusion, even if reporting on crimes may, to some extent, teach potential criminals, the positive impacts of such reports outweigh the negative impacts, especially in the current fast-changing digital era. However, certain improvements are necessary to ensure that media reports on crimes are accurate, balanced, and do not incite further crimes.

task2.prompt: It must be a woman who stays at home to care for children. Men are not suited to this kind of work. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
task2.sample: Traditionally in many parts of the world, it has been women who have stayed at home to care for children. This has led to the ideology and expectation that women are more suited to this type of work than men.The overwhelming status quo where women stay at home to care for the children probably derives from the fact that women are the ones who have to actually give birth to children and, following that, they are the ones who for the early part of a child’s life have to feed the child until it is weaned. In times past, this state of affairs probably led to the women assuming the permanent role of carer for the home and children, whilst men went out to work, whether it was to gather food or work in fields or factories.In spite of the fact that this became what was expected in family dynamics, it does not mean that men are necessarily less suited to caring for a child than women. It is very possible for men to care for a child, even from birth onwards in today’s world. Babies’ milk formula can be mixed by anyone and fed to a child. The fact that many women today choose not to do this again does not mean that they are better suited by nature to care for the child.Suitability for childcare is a matter for individual temperament and aptitude. Not many people, whether they are men or women, feel totally confident and knowledgeable about how to care for a baby or young child at the start. They need advice from their own mothers and fathers, midwives or from books. It is only from experience that skill with childcare comes and this skill can be acquired regardless of gender.All in all, I do not agree with the statement that men are less suited to childcare than women. I believe that aptitude to look after children is a matter of individual temperament, not gender-specific inherited qualities.

task2.prompt: Some people think that children should be taught at school to recycle material and avoid waste. Other believe that should be taught at home. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

Many people think that children should be taught in school to recycle unused material, while others say that this training should be given at home. This article will discuss both views before a final statement.



On the one hand, the major benefit of teaching students about reusing material and avoiding junk at school is the expertise of mentors. In other words, teachers are trained professionals who can effectively communicate the principles of recycling and staying away from waste to students. Moreover, schools provide a structured and organized learning environment where children can receive formal education on various subjects, including recycling. For example, in international-level schools like DPS, teachers use a variety of graphs and pictures to give a demonstration to younger ones so that they can understand every aspect of recycling with the help of visuals and put it into practice in their lives. Thus, providing guidance to students about recycling material and avoiding waste is beneficial.



On the other hand, progenitors play a significant role in shaping their juvenile’s values and habits. Put differently, children are more likely to adopt the behaviour of recycling and avoid using waste and carry it into adulthood when parents actively practice and teach recycling at residence . In addition, learning about recycling at home can be more flexible and adapted to individual family routines and lifestyles. Parents can give the lessons to suit the child's age and level of understanding. For instance, mentors can aware their kids about worthless goods such as plastic items, and cardboard items, which are also found at residences, and have ceased to be used. Hence, progenitors can offer a real-world demonstration of the principles of recycling.



In conclusion, having engaged in the subject, in my opinion, schools should include recycling education in their curriculum; nevertheless, parents must actively participate in teaching and practising recycling at home to their adolescents.

task2.prompt: It is a good idea to have large public spaces in towns and cities such as parks and squares. Do you agree or disagree? Why?

task2.prompt: In many countries, governments spemd large amounts of money on the arts and this is supported by some taxpayers as worthwhile. Others, however think that this money would be better spent on health and education. To what extent do you agree or disagree with these opinions? Discuss, based on your knowledge and experience.
task2.sample:
Some people adhere to the opinion that governments should financially support arts and other related activities and programmes. They feel that art enormously influences the society by transforming point of views, instilling values and interpreting experiences. Moreover, they also think that it significantly affects the fundamental sense of self.



Furthermore, they argue that arts preserve history by reminiscing an experience in a particular time and place. This can be evidenced by the massive number of paintings, sculptures, songs, literary works and other crafts, which are frequently considered as the repository of the collective memory of a society. Additionally, some researchers conducted a study of the relationship between the arts and the brain. They discovered that visual art observations had constructive effects on the personal lives of the nursing home-bound elders. In addition to this, arts can be an important key in a community's economic development. To illustrate, the arts and cultural industries provide employments, attract investors and stimulate local economies through tourism, consumer purchases and tax revenues. 



Conversely, in spite of the contributions of arts in the society, I believe that national funds should be focusing more on health and education sectors. Without a doubt, a nation can only be sustained if its citizens are well-educated and holistically healthy and fit. For instance, with the tremendous global modernization, people of various nationalities should be globally competitive enough to catch up with vast technological innovations, which are being used by large companies; so as to strengthen their workforce. Another example would be the fact that, currently, countries all over the world are in a race to purchase millions of vaccines for a particular viral disease. For this reason, governments are now allocating billions of dollars to have their vulnerable citizens vaccinated as soon as possible. Ultimately, with sufficient subsidization on health and education, societies can have lower crime rates, better overall health and civic involvement.



To sum up, arts are indeed a noteworthy representation of a country, which also aid in economic development. However, I believe that in order to enhance everyone's quality of life, create a more civilized and safer community and provide comfort others could not obtain, health care and educational systems must be financially sustained and prioritize over the others.

task2.prompt: Some experts believe that when a country is already rich, any additional increase in economic wealth does not make its citizens any more satisfied. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
task2.sample:
Some experienced individuals argue that any added wealth in a nation that is already well-off in its economy does not further satisfy its people. I completely coincide with this statement, for the reasons that, I believe a person by nature aims to be the most exceptional amongst different nationalities, and the continuous surge of payable bills.

To begin with, people by nature normally seek to be the best or have the most of things. It's not surprising that individuals tend to seek a better life, despite that they are in an advanced and wealthy economy; for the reason that they want to excel and in compete with other individuals, apart from that, if they tend to be seen that they have the best of everything, they can be adored by many. Take a person a person who is born and raised in a first-world country for example, chances are they have a much better way of life but are still unsatisfied with what they have.

Another justification for this is that the exponential allocation of finances is quite challenging to meet. Even though a country is developed and well-financed by its respective government, prices of commodities and taxes come up too. Most people in the marginalized group end up having a laborious way to pay off their bills, hence the way of life they experience is unfulfilled and affects the supposed perfect moment they should spend with their family. Take a low-wage worker for instance, they will have to spend more working hours than their expected agreement; instead of being with their nearest and dearest during their off, they tend to work more to pay their bills.

In conclusion, I ultimately agree that residents in a developed country no matter how affluent the economy is; a human being is not easily pleased because of the notion to be the best among others, and working countless hours to pay for staggering daily expenses.

task2.prompt:
In some countries, more and more people are becoming interested in finding out abou the history of the house or building they live in.

What are the reasons for this? How can people research for this?
task2.sample:
Discovering the historical background of houses or building individuals live in has become an interesting thing for more and more citizens in several countries. There are many reasons for this phenomenon and different ways for residents to research these backgrounds.



The main reason why many citizens are eager to learn the story of the place where they live is that they want to strengthen the bond between them and the property. Nowadays, the time of changing places of living increases a lot, since there are lots of reasons for moving to another location. For example, millions of college graduates need to start a brand new life in another city by renting a house. The frequent transformation would lead to unfamiliarity with the construction they stayed, and understanding its history would be a perfect method to get to know the building. Another reason is that the stories behind the construction are often pretty fascinating. For instance, the department where my sister stays used to belong to a famous doctor in the city.



To research information about buildings, we can search on the Internet to find the constructors and the owners who used to possess the real estate. Maybe some background stories can also be discovered on the website. Moreover, interviewing such related people is another way to specify the things that happened where we now dwell. For example, my sister didn't know the fact that a famous doctor used to own the residence until she talked with her neighbours.



In conclusion, newcomers are passionate about the legend behind the place they inhabit in because they want to learn more about the site they choose to linger in. Searching on the website and interviewing individuals related to the building are the main ways to learn about such information.

task2.prompt: Some people think that art is an essential subject for children at school while others it is a waste of time. Discuss both sides and give your opinion.
task2.sample:
There is a section of society that considers it absolutely necessary to teach students art related subjects at school. On the other hand, some are of the view that art related subjects are frivolous, futile and unproductive. So, instead of squandering time on such subjects, time should be spent on other productive subjects so that it could be optimally utilized. Before giving my opinion, I would like to discuss both views. 
On one hand, there are people who regard art as a redundant subject. Perhaps, such people are of the opinion that by studying art, students would not be able to acquire any practical skill and cannot make a stable career out of it thus rendering it an unrewarding subject. For instance, if someone studies subjects like science, mathematics or computer, these subjects would equip him with the skills required in the job market and he would be able to compete and pursue a successful career by studying aforesaid subjects whereas art may be good for nothing. 
On the contrary, there are people who believe that it is extremely important to impart art education to students at school. There are various reasons to substantiate this argument. First and foremost is that art plays a vital role in personality development of a student. It helps enhance creativity and hone problem solving skills. There are various research reports published by reputed institutions which corroborate this fact. Moreover, it is a prevalent notion that artists are often not paid well which is not the case. In the modern era, the advancement in technology and explosive growth of the internet has created a plethora of opportunities for digital designers, multimedia artists and animators. Furthermore, students studying diverse subjects can benefit from interdisciplinary studies. They can apply their knowledge from one discipline to solve problems of other subjects, consequently maximizing their learning experience. 
This has lead me to conclude that art is of paramount significance for a school going child as it helps foster creativity and innovation, creates a diverse learning experience. It can also lead to a successful career. Therefore, significance of art as a subject for school going children cannot be undermined.

task2.prompt: In some cities people are choosing cars instead of bicycles, while in other cities riding bikes are replacing cars. Why is this the case? Which development do you think is better?
task2.sample:
It is believed by some people that driving vehicles are the first choice when they go out. Others, on the contrary, think that riding bicycles are prioritised. This essay will introduce reasons of the trend and give my opinions.

Travelling by bikes have two advantages.Firstly,it is good for our health. The bicycle is an environment-friendly transportation as it never needs fuel, which causes no pollutants in the air. As the result, the risk of several diseases may be decreased. Secondly, Riding bicycles will save time in short distance route. There are always a large number of vehicles on the roads, especially during the rush hours in the big cities such as New York and Beijing. Instead of driving cars, riding bikes significantly reduce the traffic congestion and help residents save a lot of time in commuting.

It is also reasonable as why cars are popular in some cities. It is widely known that driving is more efficient, particularly in long distance journey. Nowadays, more and more people would like to broaden views and explore new things by tourism. Comparing with the bikes, cars which do not require a lot of energy from travellers and are much faster can save a lot of time and give explorers more opportunities to views more places and scenery. 

In conclusion, in my mind, both approaches have their own pros and cons. There is no good or bad choice, It all depends on personal preference. Cycling can not only curb the carbon emissions but also help people in keeping both physical and mental health. Meanwhile, cars, in developing countries, can give people higher social status and provide a more efficient way for people to achieve the destination.

task2.prompt: Pollution and other environmental damages are caused by a country developing and becoming richer. This problem cannot be avoided. To what extent do you agree?

Some people argue that to become prosperous, growing nations are responsible for contaminating the atmosphere and consider it is an unavoidable factor. This essay disagrees that a country cannot grow without creating pollution and affecting its surroundings. Firstly, this essay will discuss about the possibilities of development with the use of eco-friendly system and followed by tree plantation is spite of industrialization at large extent.
To begin with, the development can also be possible with the adoption of eco-friendly techniques. There is no doubt that in the race of becoming privileged, most of the nations are adopting cheapest sources like fossil fuels for their convenience.Conversely, they can use renewable sources of energy such as solar systems, wind power plants, et cetera for the generation of energy. Even though the maintenance and implementation of such resources are expensive, but are pollution free. For instance, economically rich nations such as the USA, the UK, Canada, Australia and Dubai adopt advanced methods of technology by prioritizing their environment than latest inventions.
On the other hand, despite of industrialization, large number of tree plantation can also help in eliminating the problems related to air pollution. To eliminate such harmful effects of technology, heavy mass of trees should be planted to improve the air quality. The survey, conducted by The Times India stated that in the international index of air quality, most of the rich countries are in the top list among those countries which are implementing environmental friendly methods in the research of advanced developments.
In conclusion, most people thought that growing nation cannot become wealthy without harming their surroundings. However, to prevent from the dangerous effects of non-renewable resources, people can move towards an environmentally friendly system like solar power plants, to generate power. Additionally, growing a large number of trees is the best way to avoid destruction of environment in modern industrialization era.

On the one hand, there are those who think that the authorities can impose strict guidelines on food companies in order to enhance public health. This is because if some food companies and restaurants are not providing food up to the government’s standard, then strict action should be taken against those. For instance, it has been found in a recent survey by The Sunday Times that peoples’ health can significantly be improved when the government imposes strict laws on food companies about the nutritious value of their food items. However, I disagree with this viewpoint because of the following reason.



On the other hand, it is thought that men and women can improve their health standards on their own. For example, I was a fatty person and used to eat junk food daily. But when I started doing exercise and eating healthy food by making changes in my lifestyle, I have become a healthy person. Therefore, I believe that someone’s health depends on their own by altering their lifestyle.



In conclusion, although the government can make laws to boost public health, I believe that it is a person’s responsibility to become healthy by changing the way of living their life.

The main reason why most traditional customs are worth keeping is that they are still useful in the modern world. While some traditional customs including unconditionally following policies made by the king have been replaced by the democratic political system, there are still quite some traditional customs that adapt well to modern society. For example, people in east asian countries are still used to shaking hands when they meet new friends or business partners, which has been followed for more than 1000 years and is still a great way to help quickly establish friendship or business cooperation. Consequently, those kinds of traditional customs should be kept.



Another important reason for keeping certain traditional customs and behaviours is that they are essential records of human history. For instance, in the Western world, people celebrate Christmas and in many countries in East Asia and Southeast Asia such as China and Vietnam, people celebrate Lunar New Year, which gathers family members together and reminds people of the history of their ancestors. These traditional customs have built a bridge between modern civilization and ancient history, which is a priceless treasure in human beings’ history. Therefore, it is important to preserve some traditional customs.



In conclusion, although some outdated traditional customs deserve to be abandoned in the modern world, I firmly believe that some traditional customs are vital parts of human history and are still applicable in modern society and thus should be kept.

task2.prompt: Human activities have negative effects on plant and animal species . Some Human activities have negative effects on plant and animal species. From my perspective, I have a strong belief that several measures can be taken to solve this dilemma.



To begin with, some people have the right reasons to claim that it is an unsolvable problem and that nothing can be done to deal with it. Deforestation or climate change caused by human activities is so destructive that it is placing many species' lives at risk. As a consequence, many species of plants and animals are dying due to loss of habitat and human hunt. Some of them have already become extinct, thus negatively affecting the balance of the ecosystem. For example, in Vietnam where there used to be a large number of tigers, this animal has been hunted for years to satisfy human needs and there are only a few species left. 



However, I strongly argue that there are a lot of things that governments and individuals can do to deal with this issue. Firstly, the issue of deforestation needs to be addressed. It is the main cause of the disappearance of endangered species around the world. Governments can plant more trees to create places for animals and plants to live and develop their population. Moreover, strict rules should be published to deter people from cutting down trees and hunting for precious animals and plants. Another solution is to raise awareness among residents about the destructive effects of our activities on the Earth and the ecosystem. In conclusion, while some damage is irreversible, it is not too late to take effective measures to improve the situation. task2.prompt:

task2.prompt: Some people today believe that it is acceptable to use physical force to discipline children, but others feel it is completely unacceptable.Discuss this view and give your opinion.
task2.sample: Punishing children with physical force, or corporal punishment as it is also called, is something that was accepted not so long ago and people over the age of forty may well remember it. Nowadays, however, corporal punishment is against the law in most countries and adults who practise it can be taken to court. Children are always a vulnerable group and they depend on adults for protection and education. Of course, part of the growing up process is testing and breaking boundaries and it is nearly always necessary to instill discipline on a child. Whether or not it is necessary to use physical force to do so can be a very emotive subject.Supporters of corporal punishment often defend their standpoint by explaining that the corporal punishment is not, or should not be, excessive. They do not argue that a child should be beaten severely until he or she is bruised or cut. They argue that just the infliction of mild pain causes effective discipline and also the fear that it might be applied. People who grew up experiencing it might offer this point of view.Those who oppose using physical force on a child would say that the vulnerability and innocence of a child means that force should never be used. Children need to trust adults and believe that no harm will come to them. Additionally, children learn from adults and it is argued that corporal punishment will only teach children that force is an answer to various problems. It is also claimed that corporal punishment has no added benefits over other forms of discipline that do not require physical force. Using it can cause psychological harm to children and should be classed as child abuse.Personally, I do not believe that limited use of forms of corporal punishment can cause harm, and a parent who administers a mild form of it to his or her child should not be subject to criminal proceedings. Nevertheless, I would not use it myself. I can also recognise the possibilities of adults who are not a child’s parents misusing corporal punishment. Therefore, I believe that on balance physical force to discipline children should not be permitted.

In conclusion, it is obvious that reducing the cost of operating power is such a debated issue to solve the environmental problem. task2.prompt: Some people believe that the best way to solve environmental problems is to increase the price of fuel.Do you agree or disagree?
task2.sample: Raising the price of car fuel is believed by some people to be an excellent method to solve the growing number of environmental issues. While making fuel more expensive wouldn’t change the habits of wealthy families, switching to fossil fuel alternatives could prove to be much more beneficial for the environment.The most compelling reason against raising the cost of fuel is that the upper classes of society will hardly be affected by rising fuel costs, as this only makes up a minor proportion of their expenditure. They will continue to use their personal vehicles as they wish without a thought for the environment or the higher fuel prices, even if their country has state-of-the-art public transportation.Those who will feel the crunch of this decision are the middle-class and lower-income households, since travelling is a major part of most people’s routine, be it to work, school or shopping. Driving is almost unavoidable in many instances; therefore, raising the price of petrol would only serve to widen the gap between the rich and poor, and serve as an inadvertent form of discrimination.Another reason why increasing the cost of fuel is far from the best way to deal with environmental pollution is that now there are much more viable alternatives. Due to the rapid advances in technology, scientists and engineers have been able to develop several alternatives to fossil fuel, such as cars powered by electricity or naturally produced biofuel. The move to adopt clean energy sources instead of fossil fuels is a much more promising alternative compared to simply making fuel more expensive.In conclusion, I believe that governments of the world should invest more time and money in finding alternatives to fossil fuels that are more environmentally friendly, rather than simply raising the cost of petrol.

In conclusion, although it is argued that the duty of preserving the environment should fall to one international organization instead of local governments, I do believe that this phenomenon should be coped with together to get the maximum effects.

Furthermore, using public transportations rather than private vehicles for commuting would significantly alleviate our carbon footprint. Therefore, if humans shift to renewable and recyclable materials then it would drastically minimise the temperature rising issues.
To conclude, people's actions that change the environment have a negative impact on the global climate. However, we can substantially lessen it by curbing fossil fuels and plastic usage.

task2.prompt: In many different countries, most shops and products become the same. Some people think it is a positive development, while others think it is a negative development. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

This essay explores both perspectives, highlighting the advantages and drawbacks of the homogenized trend worldwide and ultimately providing a balanced viewpoint.



Advocates of the globalization of shops and products argue that it brings several advantages. Firstly, standardization enhances convenience for consumers who travel frequently or live in multiple countries. Familiarity with brand names and product offerings across borders allows customers to make informed choices without the burden of cultural or linguistic barriers. Secondly, uniformity often gives rise to improved quality control, as global brands strive to maintain consistent standards worldwide, ensuring customer satisfaction and loyalty. Thirdly, the homogenization of production can contribute to economies of scale, resulting in lower production costs and more affordable prices for consumers. In this sense, the prevalence of the similarity promotes accessibility and affordability, ultimately benefiting consumers on a global scale.



On the other hand, opponents of global sameness in shopping and production raise valid concerns. The saturation of international brands can result in the extinction of local businesses and traditional products. As global corporations dominate the market, smaller, locally-owned businesses struggle to compete, depriving communities of their unique identity and cultural heritage. Furthermore, the standardization of goods may lead to a loss of diversity in consumer choices. While convenience is favoured by some, others may argue that the charm of exploring new and unique items diminishes as the market becomes saturated with the same offerings. This can induce cultural assimilation, eroding the rich and diverse traditions that make each country unique.



In conclusion, the homogenization of shops and products is a multifaceted development that elicits diverse reactions. Embracing its advantages while mitigating its negative consequences is crucial for ensuring a sustainable global market that celebrates diversity and fosters cultural preservation.

task2.prompt: Having a salaried job is better than being self-employed. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?

task2.prompt: Some people think that range of technology currently available increasing gap between rich people and poor people . Others think that it is causing opposite effect. Discuss both views and give your opinion .
Some people believe that eventually all jobs will be done by artificial robots. What is your opinion?
task2.sample:
Nowadays, some people assume that occupations might be substituted progressively by artificial robots in the future. In my opinion, although a majority of simple jobs will be done by machines ultimately, it is impossible that positions that require human relations can be replaced. This essay will discuss the reasons why only particular tasks will be finally taken over.



Without a doubt, artificial intelligence will easily overtake jobs that do not require specific and complex human skills in the workforce. From a cost point of view, many companies will choose to use robots because it is far less expensive than training and employing a human. Cashiers in supermarkets, for instance, are gradually being replaced by checkout machines that cost far less than employees. Customers can easily pay for their goods by using self-checkout facilities rather than standing in a long queue to wait for services at a counter. For these reasons, using advanced technology can be a significantly effective way for companies. 



Conversely, there are some complicated human tasks that will never be overtaken by artificial intelligence because robots do not have the capacity to accomplish. In other words, some particular occupations require complex and critical thinking that only the human brain can implement. For example, science-related careers, such as doctors, scientists, pharmacists, and engineers, can only be carried out by professionals, even in the future. Therefore, Machines will not be able to sort out all of the problems which need to be overcome by humans. 



In conclusion, with the development of advanced artificial technology, it is no doubt that robots have the ability to replace a significant number of occupations in the near future. Unskilled labour will eventually be done by machines entirely; however, some sophisticated fields that require specific and complicated human skills will always exist. Consequently, jobs in particular professional areas will be safe in an increasingly artificial intelligent world.
